Posted November 17, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

Consider that the Canadian Medical Association has called for the decriminalization of cannabis. The CMA has even acknowledged that at least 400,000 Canadians use cannabis for medical reasons.
See
 Journal of Canadian Medical Association Calls for Decriminalization. Perfect Timing. Contrast with DEAland.
and links

The CMA also recognizes that the health effects of moderate cannabis use are " minimal " and that the real harm is caused by the legal and social consequences of prohibition. It says, " About half of all drug arrests in Canada are for simple possession of small amounts of marijuana... Many lead to jail terms or fines and all result in that indelible social tattoo: a criminal record. "

Yes, some Canadians still go to jail for simple possession.

The CMA recognizes that cannabis is also far less addictive and far less subject to abuse than many prescription drugs, such as muscle relaxants, and analgesics.
See
 Marijuana Isn't Harmless. Okay, But Why Isn't It Sold Over the Counter? Or Would You Ban Something That Causes 300,000 ER Visits Every Year, And Kills A Child Every Month? (Trick Question)

Nonetheless, the CMA and its provincial affiliates still refuse to cooperate with the patients groups in promoting an effective medical cannabis for Canadians.

Now, in that context, consider that the only people who have difficulty getting cannabis are the sick and dying. Indeed, in the ultimate perversity, the sicker someone is the harder it will be for them to get into the black market. A healthy teenager will have the easiest time getting cannabis.

Two press releases this week demonstrate the absurdity of the present situation, especially in Canada.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Monday, November 15th, 2004

Press Statement from the Meduser Group which is comprised of 15 percent of the patients participating in Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' medical marijuana access program.
See
 Health Canada Escalates Its War on the Sick and Dying as the Canadian Cannabis War Heats Up. Challenges Set In the BC Courts.

This statement is our official response to Health Canada's recent proposed " Marihuana Medical Access Regulations " amendments, which were published in the Canada Gazette.

(Vol. 138, No. 43 - October 23, 2004)

It is our position that Health Canada fails to address the needs and concerns of patients regarding medical cannabis access.

OFFICIAL STATEMENT

Regulations Amending the Marihuana Medical Access Regulations

November 15, 2004
Medusers Group Response to Health Canada on MMAR Amendments and Health Canada's Long-Term Vision of the MMAR

While it is acknowledged that Health Canada has invited patients to the table to participate and provide input on the MMAR program, Health Canada has failed in implementing these recommendations, based on patients' needs as the primary stakeholders in this program.

Health Canada is ignoring input, recommendations and rulings made by patients, the Canadian Senate Committee and the courts.
See
 Hypocrisy and Democracy: Raid on Medical Cannabis Research Facility Critical of Health Canada's Schwag Challenges Canada's Values. What Will The Politicians Say?

According to Health Canada's own information, " The main objective of this initiative, undertaken by Health Canada, is to respond to concerns expressed by the stakeholders in the medical marihuana program. " Health Canada's position is that the desires of physicians and law enforcement are more important than the needs of patients.

The physicians, CMA and CMPA have announced in writing that they want no part in their role as gatekeepers to medical cannabis access. Health Canada also states, " Physicians have expressed concern that, under the MMAR, they have been assigned a 'gatekeeper' role that they find difficult to fulfil due to the lack of scientific information available concerning the use of marihuana for specific medical purposes. "

The result of this position is that MMAR and Office of Cannabis Medical Access program remains an ineffective, cumbersome and faulty program.

There is sufficient evidence, based on Health Canada's Office of Cannabis Medical Access' statistics which reveal a constant decrease in patients enrolled in the MMAR program, that the government's medical cannabis access program is failing.

There are continuing admission problems for those wishing to enter the MMAR program, and there are continuing cannabis supply problems for those already within the system.

In addition to the MMAR admission and supply problems, Health Canada's long-term vision of phasing out personal and designated medical cannabis production licences is unacceptable, and will not be tolerated by patients who wish to cultivate their own supply of medical cannabis.

In personal health issues, freedom of choice is a fundamental right of the patient, and must be respected by Health Canada in all aspects of MMAR policy implementation. The right to produce one's supply of medical cannabis must not be hindered, and there is no reasonable justification by the government to take away this option.

This only furthers the evidence that Health Canada is not listening to, nor addressing the rights and needs of patients.

It is clear that Health Canada's position regarding medical cannabis access, is to erode the fundamental right of a patient to use this alternative natural health product.

Health Canada's vision of the medical cannabis access program is not realistically aligned with patients' requirements of timely and affordable access to multiple strains of medical cannabis. This includes a wide range of cannabis product choice - in quality, source and price to meet a patient's individual needs.

The recent proposed MMAR amendments fail to address the primary intent of the MMAR program, which is to provide people who wish to use cannabis medicinally with efficient compassionate access to a range of safe and effective sources of marihuana.

Health Canada continues to ignore these requirements, and it is evident from the lack of action in acknowledging and addressing these concerns, that the needs of patients are not a priority in MMAR policy development and amendments.

November 17, 2004
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

SURVEY SHOWS MARIJUANA LAWS A TOTAL FAILURE

OTTAWA A landmark survey released today by the Canadian Centre for Substance Abuse (CCSA) shows that the use of marijuana is at all time record levels. The Canadian Addiction Survey, the first major study of the issue in a decade, reveals that criminalizing marijuana has not deterred Canadians from using it. In fact, it has done the opposite.

According to the survey, usage rates among young people have doubled over the last ten years. All the laws and the hundreds of millions of dollars given to police enforcement towards deterrence have been an abysmal waste of time and money. The survey shows that today 70% of 18 to 24 year olds admit to having used marijuana in their lifetime.

Usage rates are soaring even as the government continues to pour hundreds of millions of dollars each year to enforce our marijuana laws. The Canadian Addiction Survey also reveals that 44.5% of Canadians admit to using marijuana in their lifetime and 14.1% of Canadians admitting to use in the past year. 54% of the over three million Canadians admitting use in the last year describe their use as monthly, weekly, or daily.
See
 Good News From Holland Is Even Better in Context. Large Majority of Dutch Parliament Favors Legalization of Cannabis. Most EU Countries Recognize Dutch Model Superior to DEAland's. We Are Winning!

" Criminal prosecution and enforcement has only led to increased consumption of marijuana. We need a smarter strategy, starting with the recognition that the current approach has failed, " said Jody Pressman, Executive Director of NORML Canada. Criminalizing use has ruined people's lives, cost hundreds of millions, and only served to fatten police budgets and the profit margin for organized crime.

The government recently reintroduced Bill C-17, legislation that would continue to criminalize marijuana use despite evidence that this approach exacerbates usage rates rather than reduces them.
See
 Arresting Developments: 2003 Cannabis Arrests Hit All-Time High In DEAland, Decline In UK and Canada. Deaths Related to One Drug Soar In Holland. Guess Which One.

Over three million Canadians use marijuana and they are tired of being treated like criminals. Government is out of touch with public opinion on marijuana, said Pressman. Instead of perpetuating the failed policies of the past, NORML Canada calls on government to regulate and tax marijuana like beer, wine, and spirits.
